newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan to issue 2-, 3-yr T-bills from June.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan to issue 2-, 3-yr T-bills from June.

text.p: Kazakhstan's government will extend the maturity of its domestic debt by issuing two and three-year Treasury bills, with the first auction of the new paper held later this month, Finance Minister Alexander Pavlov said on Thursday.

"Now we are turning to longer debt issues -- two- and three-year securities. These will be discount papers like current T-bills, and will also be sold at auctions," Pavlov, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, told Reuters. "The first auction will be held this month." At present the Finance Ministry holds auctions of three-, six- and 12-month T-bills.

Yields on currently traded T-bills have fallen sharply over the last few months, and dealers say that many local banks and foreign investors -- once keen buyers of Kazakh government securities -- are now eyeing T-bill markets in other countries.
"I agree that this is abnormal when T-bill yields are lower than inflation. This is why we are going to issue these two- and three-year papers," Pavlov said.

"Foreigners' participation in the last two T-bill auctions was small," National Bank Governor Uraz Dzhandosov told Reuters. Foreigners are now entitled to buy up to 30 percent of three-, six- amd 12-month paper but Dzhandosov said: "I believe we will not impose any limits on two- and three-year securities."

He said the volume of each issue of the new T-bills offered at regular auctions would total between 500 million and one billion tenge. He declined to name the date of the first auction or to say how frequently the new securities would be sold.
